chunks: One may not avail oneself of tayammum except for a single salat and its supererogatory prayer.

The first thing about this report is that it is a solitary report, and despite that, its wordings differ while the narrator is one; for Abū Hammām, in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, narrated it from al-Riḍā عليه السلام without an intermediary, while in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, it is from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Ghazwān, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Yet the ruling is one, and this weakens using it as proof. Moreover, the narrator of this report with this very isnad narrated the like of what we mentioned, namely the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb from al-ʿAbbās, from Abū Hammām, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Ghazwān, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar عليه السلام; and we have already cited it. Thus it is known thereby that what this report contains is an error from the narrator.

And even if this report is accepted, it is possible to interpret it as referring to one who later became able to use water but did not perform wudu (ablution). In that case, it is not permissible for him to make lawful for himself, by that prior tayammum, more than a single salat, and he must renew tayammum for the prayer he is yet to perform. That which indicates this is as follows.

And it was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAbbās, from Abū Hammām, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Ghazwān, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said:

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution used in place of wudu (ablution) when water cannot be used
key_terms.الْإِسْنَادِ: the chain of narrators transmitting the report
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, whose availability affects the validity of continuing with tayammum
key_terms.سَهْوٌ: an error or lapse attributed here to the narrator
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ: a single salat, indicating the limited scope discussed in the report

ai.seo_question: Can one perform multiple prayers with a single tayammum according to this narration in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a report concerning whether tayammum may be used for more than one salat, and it critiques the report on hadith-transmission grounds because of inconsistencies in its wording and chain. It then offers a reconciliation: if a person later becomes able to use water and does not perform wudu (ablution), the earlier tayammum does not permit more than one salat.
